title: E0035: Missing Array Key
plain_english: Reports reads of keys that are missing from tracked literal arrays.
why_matters: Accessing a missing array key can produce warnings/notices and lead to unexpected `null` values. This rule uses Phanalist's bounded formal verification engine (Z3-backed) to find feasible paths where a key read is missing.
bad_example:
<?php
/** @param array{name: string} $user */
function greet(array $user): string
{
    return $user['email']; // key may be missing
}
good_example:
<?php
/** @param array{name: string, email?: string} $user */
function greet(array $user): string
{
    $email = $user['email'] ?? 'unknown';

    return $email;
}
what_it_checks: Missing string and integer keys in tracked literal arrays
Keys returned by `array_key_first()` and `array_key_last()` for tracked literal arrays, preserving PHP insertion order
Arrays forgotten after writes through untracked paths or by-reference calls
Keys checked through bounded branches and short-circuit conditions
